tool_signatures.name: create_1
tool_signatures.description: Stores HTML or markdown content and returns a shareable link. Reuse existing owner token to group entities under one owner. Also accepts raw text/* (HTML, Markdown, YAML, XML, CSV, code) and application/octet-stream bodies — see /llms-full.txt. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password.

ns.description: Send ns=public for anything meant to be found or shared (docs, guides, demos, portfolios, reports, landing pages): listed in the public gallery and sitemap, so Google, Bing and AI search index it and people discover it. Public pages are served on the brewpage.app domain itself, for the strongest search reach; code that needs its own origin (cookies, storage) gets its own subdomain automatically. Anyone can find and read a public page: never put secrets, tokens or personal data there. No ns (default): private. Unlisted and not indexed; anyone who has the link can still open it. Lowercase only.

ttl.description: TTL in days: up to 30 days without an account, up to 90 with a free profile (send its X-Owner-Token); a default applies when `ttl` is omitted. Accepts whole days: 15, 15d, 15 days.

format.description: Optional content format, same values as the 'format' query param. Takes precedence over the query param when both are present.

X-Password.description: Access password. Empty means no password restriction. Protected pages are never listed in the gallery or sitemap. OLD links accept ?p=; NEW access uses X-Password or a reader access cookie after password entry.

verbatim.description: Store the content exactly as sent. By default a whole HTML page pasted from a chat (wrapped in a code block, surrounded by chat text, or entity-escaped) is restored and a notice is returned; 'true' keeps the text as is.

domain.description: Custom domain to connect to the new publication, e.g. www.example.com or example.com (query parameter or form/multipart field). Needs an X-Owner-Token added to a free BrewPage profile; works for HTML pages of format html and for sites, without a password. The publication is always created; on success the answer carries `customDomain` with the DNS `records[]` to create; then call POST /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain/check once and read GET /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain until `status` is `active`. Otherwise one notice says why it was not set: domain-needs-account, domain-limit-reached, domain-not-eligible, domain-invalid, domain-not-registered, domain-account-restricted, domain-profile-ambiguous or domain-unavailable. Updates ignore it (notice domain-ignored): use PUT /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain.

JSON body only; invalid settings answer 400 and nothing is published.

tool_signatures.name: upload
tool_signatures.description: Stores a file via multipart upload and returns a download link. Only safe file types accepted; a missing or wrong extension is corrected from the content and reported in notices. Reuse existing owner token to group entities under one owner. An HTML or Markdown file is published as a page in any namespace, with or without a password (same rules and limits as POST /api/html). 'format' decides; without one a known extension, then a specific declared part type (text/html, text/markdown, application/json, text/csv), then a content guess; otherwise it stays an inert file. '.txt' without 'format' stays a text file. A whole HTML document sent as 'markdown' is an HTML page. Any readable encoding is stored as UTF-8, notice 'charset-guessed' when no usable charset was named. link and ownerLink point to the page, notice 'html-file-as-page' or 'markdown-file-as-page'; a code format chosen by 'format' or the declared type is published the same way, notice 'file-format-applied'. An HTML file over the page size limit or that no encoding reads is stored as a file and shown as source, notice 'html-file-as-source'. A JSON file in the public namespace is stored as sent, notice 'json-file-not-listed'; JSON data belongs in POST /api/json. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password.

ns.description: Send ns=public for anything meant to be found or shared (docs, guides, demos, portfolios, reports, landing pages): listed in the public gallery and sitemap, so Google, Bing and AI search index it and people discover it. Public pages are served on the brewpage.app domain itself, for the strongest search reach; code that needs its own origin (cookies, storage) gets its own subdomain automatically. Anyone can find and read a public page: never put secrets, tokens or personal data there. No ns (default): private. Unlisted and not indexed; anyone who has the link can still open it. Lowercase only.

format.description: Format of a page published from this file: decides over the file name. Unknown values are ignored.

ttl.description: TTL in days: up to 30 days without an account, up to 90 with a free profile (send its X-Owner-Token); a default applies when `ttl` is omitted. Accepts whole days: 15, 15d, 15 days.

verbatim.description: For an HTML file published as a page: store it exactly as sent. By default a whole HTML page pasted from a chat (wrapped in a code block, surrounded by chat text, or entity-escaped) is restored and a notice is returned; 'true' keeps the text as is.

parameters.name: ns
parameters.description: Send ns=public for anything meant to be found or shared (docs, guides, demos, portfolios, reports, landing pages): listed in the public gallery and sitemap, so Google, Bing and AI search index it and people discover it. Public pages are served on the brewpage.app domain itself, for the strongest search reach; code that needs its own origin (cookies, storage) gets its own subdomain automatically. Anyone can find and read a public page: never put secrets, tokens or personal data there. No ns (default): private. Unlisted and not indexed; anyone who has the link can still open it. Lowercase only.

parameters.name: ttl

parameters.name: verbatim
parameters.description: For an HTML file published as a page: store it exactly as sent. By default a whole HTML page pasted from a chat (wrapped in a code block, surrounded by chat text, or entity-escaped) is restored and a notice is returned; 'true' keeps the text as is.
